ads_ratio.reason: Engine per-share figures are per ordinary share while the traded NYSE price ($70.07) is per ADS; without the ratio every per-share comparison is understated 3x.
ads_ratio.source: Woori Financial Group's own SEC filings (CIK 1264136): Form 20-F filer whose ADS registration statement on Form F-6 states 'American Depositary Shares (ADSs), each ADS representing three (3) Shares of Common Stock, par value 5,000 Won per share'; the NYSE security name itself is 'American Depositary Shares (each representing three (3) shares of Common Stock)'.

moat_against: Commoditized products: no pricing-power differentiation vs KB Financial, Shinhan and Hana
Earnings tied to the Korean credit cycle, real-estate PF exposure and household-debt regulation
Net interest margin pressure and policy caps on household lending limit the core spread business
KRW/USD exposure for ADS holders: won weakness directly cuts USD-translated earnings
Structurally low bank ROE economics; growth ceiling set by a mature domestic market
moat_for: Licensed major-bank franchise: regulatory barriers and systemic importance in Korean banking
Large domestic deposit base and nationwide branch/digital network via Woori Bank
Diversification improving: non-bank units (securities, card, capital, Tongyang Life) reached 22.3% of H1 2026 net profit
CET1 ratio 13.71% (Q2 2026) supports sustained dividends and buybacks, incl. treasury-share cancellation resolved Jul 2026
moat_justification: Woori is one of Korea's four major financial holding companies, anchored by Woori Bank. Korean retail/commercial banking is a regulated, scale-driven but largely commoditized business in a mature, slow-growth market: the license and deposit franchise are real barriers, but Woori has no durable pricing-power or cost edge over KB, Shinhan and Hana, earnings ride the Korean credit cycle and regulator policy (household-debt caps, NIM pressure), and returns are capped by low-ROE banking economics. Non-bank diversification is improving (22.3% of H1 2026 net profit vs 6.9% a year earlier) but is not yet a moat. Score 3/10 = weak moat; CAP = 5.9 years.
name: Woori Financial Group Inc.
one_liner: Weak-moat (3/10) Korean big-four bank holding company; the OCF-based OE model fits banks poorly (sector mismatch) and even the normalized per-ADS base of $4.46 produces only an 8.9% weighted IRR at $70.07 — Tier D. It would clear the 15% hurdle only at or below the weighted IV@15 of $35.82, roughly half the current ADS price.
